subject: OrbitCare private: sudden throughput collapse & leadership pulse
messages:
From: OrbitCare Ops <ops@orbitcare.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina@orbitcare.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: private cluster throughput collapse impacting inference pipelines

Vanessa / Marissa —

We started seeing sustained throughput drops across our on-prem cluster in the NightOps window (01:30–03:40 PT). p50 is up ~3x and p95/p99 have spiked; many small single-request batches are timing out at the runtime layer. Attach snapshots attached (throughput_snap_2028-04-01.png).

Impact: several downstream inference jobs (clinical triage routing) have delayed completions and a 10% failure rate on retries. This is directly impacting patient triage SLA (30m).

What we see from our side:
- Sudden increase in small-batch single-token requests routed to the private cluster.
- Runtime logs show repeated kv-cache miss/eviction warnings and kernel fallback to slower paths.
- No config changes on our cluster in the window; we did push an updated model variant (8-bit quantized) three days ago.

We need a prioritized action plan and an exec sync (we can make time today). Please advise next steps and temporary mitigations (routing to hosted/dedicated, rate limiting, warmup).

Thanks,
--
OrbitCare NightOps Team
ops@orbitcare.ai

Attachments: throughput_snap_2028-04-01.png
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: OrbitCare Ops <ops@orbitcare.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: private cluster throughput collapse impacting inference pipelines

Thanks for the heads up and the graphs, Nina / Ops team. We've triaged this as high-priority. Marissa — looping you in for the customer comms. Laura / Eng — could you start an immediate investigation into runtime telemetry? Initial asks:

1) Can the runtime team confirm whether the kv-cache eviction warnings correlate with the model variant rollout?
2) Any rapid mitigations we can apply (routing small-batch traffic to Hosted or a Dedicated pool, a warmup job, or temporary throttles) that don't require customer code changes?

OrbitCare — we're proposing a short exec sync at 10:30 PT to align on the immediate mitigation and the MAP (mutual action plan). Please confirm availability.

I'll assemble a one-page briefing for the sync with the latest metrics and proposed fallbacks.

- Vanessa
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: private cluster throughput collapse impacting inference pipelines

Quick update from runtime investigation:

- Correlation: yes — the p95 spike aligns with the 8-bit quantized model rollout (04-30 deployment). We see degenerated kernel selection for short sequences: the runtime is choosing a general path that has poor small-batch perf for quantized weights.
- KV cache behavior: eviction warnings are real but secondary — root issue appears to be a code-path that avoids the quantized fast-kernel when sequence length <= 8 under certain packing heuristics. That path triggers many micro-context restarts and causes sustained small-batch CPU/GPU overhead (and I/O to address space).
- Candidate mitigations (fast):
  * Force the fast-kernel path via a rollout knob (software toggle) — low risk, requires a quick recompile or dynamic kernel switch on the nodes serving that model. Estimated lead time: 2–3 hours with a hot restart.
  * Apply a temporary traffic-split to Hosted/Dedicated for single-token/small-batch requests — requires routing rule change at the control plane, can be done in ~30–45 mins if OrbitCare is ok with routing a subset externally.
  * Warmup batch job and KV prefill for the private cluster — best when combined with the kernel switch, takes ~1 hour to warm caches.

I'm starting a jitter-free hot-redeploy plan for the affected model on a canary node. I'll share logs and a short playbook (runtime-playbook-delta.patch).

- Laura
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, OrbitCare Ops <ops@orbitcare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: private cluster throughput collapse impacting inference pipelines

OrbitCare team — from a commercial/ops perspective we can provide a temporary Dedicated pool for the next 72 hours at no charge while you and the runtime team validate the kernel toggle and warmup. We want to avoid SLA violations and give your engineers time to roll back the variant if needed. If you approve, I can open a dedicated migration ticket and coordinate traffic split with Laura.

Marissa — I'll also draft a customer note offering credits if the SLA breach exceeds the window.

Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: private cluster throughput collapse impacting inference pipelines

Thanks — high level ask from my side: please surface one pager for Execs covering 1) impact to patient-facing SLAs (quantified), 2) proposed immediate mitigation and expected RTO, 3) root cause hypothesis, 4) customer-facing MAP with timelines and ownership. I'll join the 10:30 sync (or subsequent leadership touch) and carry any ask to the CTO if we need a priority CPU/GPU kernel backport.

Also: Laura — if the fast-kernel toggle requires a kernel binary recompile, we should prioritize a static backport build that can be A/Bed quickly. Keep me posted on the canary results.

- Vivek
Director, Engineering Operations
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: OrbitCare Ops <ops@orbitcare.ai>, Nina Patel <nina@orbitcare.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: OrbitCare immediate plan and next steps (mutual action plan attached)

Nina / Ops team — thanks for the patience. Short summary and MAP: 

Summary of diagnosis (runtime): fast-kernel selection regression for short sequences interacting poorly with the new quantized model variant; secondary kv-cache eviction noise.

Immediate mitigations we agreed and started:
- Laura kicked off a canary that forces the fast-kernel path (hot restart) — monitoring p50/p95 for the node. ETA: 2–3 hours for full verification.
- Aditya activated a temporary Dedicated pool for small-batch traffic — live now; routing rule ID: JIRA-OPS-4821.
- We will run a KV prefill warmup job on private nodes to stabilize cache behavior (1 hour run).

Customer asks / deadlines:
- OrbitCare: confirm whether the transient routing to Dedicated for single-token requests is acceptable. Please respond with approval or objection by 17:30 PT so we can keep the routing in place while we validate.
- Redwood: provide an exec one-pager (attached) and a remediation ETA for a safe rollback or a permanent kernel backport.

Attachments: orbitcare_mau_q2.xlsx (customer usage), runtime-playbook-delta.patch (runtime hotfix).

Next sync: 18:00 PT for a final verification and to confirm MAP sign-off.

Thank you — we'll keep this tightly coordinated.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success | Redwood Inference
